summary: This VBScript scans the current folder for Excel files (.xlsm and .xlam), opens each one, and displays all the external references (add-ins) that file uses. It wraps Excel interaction in a class that manages opening/closing the application and workbooks cleanly, and it ensures the script runs under CScript for better console output.

explanations.13: This forces VBScript to declare all variables before using them, which catches typos and makes code more reliable.
explanations.23: This is a property setter—it lets you write `obj.verbose = True` instead of calling a method, making the code feel more natural.
explanations.30: This checks whether the oApplication variable actually points to an Excel object (not empty/null) before trying to use it.
explanations.52: This is a special method that runs automatically when you create a new instance of the class, used here to initialize all the private variables.
explanations.64: This is a special method that runs automatically when the class object is destroyed, used here to clean up and release Excel resources.
explanations.87: This tells VBScript to keep running even if the next line causes an error, so we can check if the error happened and handle it.
explanations.89: This tries to connect to an Excel application that's already running, rather than starting a brand new one.
explanations.101: This clears any error information from the previous operation so we don't accidentally react to old errors.
explanations.103: This turns error-handling back to normal (stop on any error).
explanations.156: This extracts just the filename from the full path—for example, turning 'C:\Files\myfile.xlsx' into 'myfile.xlsx'.
explanations.196: This checks if the reference's file path ends in '.xlam' (an Excel add-in file), converting to lowercase first so the comparison works regardless of uppercase/lowercase in the actual path.
explanations.239: This looks at the last 12 characters of the script's executable name to see if it says 'cscript.exe'.
explanations.244: Chr(34) is the double-quote character; this wraps each command-line argument in quotes so spaces inside arguments don't break them apart.
explanations.280: THen is a typo (should be 'Then'), but it's what the original code has.
explanations.314: This extracts just the file extension (like 'xlsm' or 'xlam') from the filename.
explanations.326: This removes the trailing '#' delimiter from the end of the concatenated string.
explanations.345: This splits the string 'file1.xlsx#file2.xlsx#file3.xlsx' into an array using '#' as the separator.
explanations.355: UBound returns the highest index in the array, so this loop processes every file from index 0 to the last one.
